prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: hire a local personal-injury attorney who specializes in car-accident cases (not a generalist), handles cases on contingency, has trial experience and good local references, and communicates clearly. If you want, I can help you create a short list of attorneys to contact or a call/email script.

To help you pick the right lawyer, tell me a few quick facts first:
- Were you injured? How serious (hospitalized, ongoing treatment, minor)?
- Was the other driver clearly at fault? Were there police/witnesses?
- Do you already have a claims adjuster or been contacted by the other party’s insurer?
- Any deadlines (surgery scheduled, insurance deadlines), or how long since the crash?
- Do you want someone near Pleasanton or willing to work remotely?

Immediate steps you should take (if you haven’t already)
1. Get medical care right away and follow up — your health and contemporaneous medical records are crucial.
2. Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, scene; contact info for witnesses; police report number.
3. Notify your auto insurer per policy terms (give facts, don’t speculate about fault).
4. Do not give recorded statements to the other side’s insurer without consulting a lawyer.
5. Keep all bills, pay stubs (if you missed work), receipts, and treatment notes.

What to look for in an attorney
- Specialization: focus on car-accident and personal-injury law.
- Experience and track record with similar cases (injury type and severity).
- Trial experience and litigation resources — many cases settle, but you want someone ready to take it to court.
- Contingency fees (you pay only if they recover money) and clear fee schedule for costs.
- Good communication: clear timeline, who handles your calls, regular updates.
- Local knowledge (Alameda County/Pleasanton courts, local medical providers).
- Client references and online reviews (read for patterns, not single bad reviews).

Questions to ask in an initial free consultation
- Do you handle car-accident injury cases in Pleasanton/Alameda County? How long have you practiced?
- How many similar cases have you handled? What were typical outcomes?
- Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your fee and who pays costs if we lose?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (you or an associate/paralegal)?
- Do you try cases? Have you gone to trial recently?
- How long do you expect my case will take? What are the likely outcomes?
- What information/documents do you need from me now?
- Can you provide client references or recent case results?

Typical fee structure (what to expect)
- Most personal-injury attorneys in CA work on contingency: commonly 33% for pre-lawsuit settlement, 33–40% if suit filed (varies).
- You may also be responsible for out-of-pocket costs (medical record retrieval, expert fees) which are often advanced by the firm and repaid from recovery.
- Get the fee agreement in writing and make sure you understand who pays what if there’s no recovery.

Time limits
- California personal-injury claims generally have a 2-year statute of limitations from the date of the accident. Don’t wait — consult an attorney promptly.

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount.
- Pressure to sign immediately without time to read the agreement.
- No clear fee agreement or unwillingness to answer basic questions.
- No phone/office contact information, poor reviews about communication.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short script/email to contact 3–5 local lawyers.
- Suggest what documents to bring to consultations.
- Help evaluate answers you get from attorneys and narrow to the best choice.

Tell me the crash details you can share (injuries, police report, insurance contact) and whether you want me to draft a contact script or list of questions to use in calls — I’ll tailor the next step.
